answer: A spectral ranking protocol curbs Sybil attacks by routing early-stopping random walks from trusted seeds across the agent graph. Each identity occupies a vertex whose score is throttled by sparse topological cuts, preventing adversaries from hiding behind a dune of fake accounts. To capture network reward nectar, an attacker must secure scarce, authentic edges with honest peers per identity. However, peripheral honest agents face false-positive rejections due to graph sparsity.
